highlights: Geopolitical risk dominates: US-Iran conflict escalates with strikes on Iran and Strait of Hormuz attacks, driving oil prices to two-week highs and triggering broad market selloff.
Tech sector under pressure: AI chip stocks (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) tumble despite strong earnings, entering bear market territory; Nasdaq-100 shows potential diamond top pattern.
Bond market selloff: Treasury two-year yield near 2026 high, reflecting inflation fears and rate uncertainty.
Defensive rotation: Investors shift to energy, utilities (Duke Energy), and infrastructure plays amid geopolitical turmoil.
AI funding boom continues: Tech companies tap debt/equity markets for AI/cloud expansion; hyperscaler debt becomes a rates story.
Consumer and housing: Mortgage rates continue falling, Walmart announces sweeping price cuts, but inflation risks from oil surge threaten consumer spending.
Regulatory and political: Democratic probe into Lutnick/Cantor Fitzgerald, new UK tax rules from 2027, USPS stamp price hike.
SpaceX enters Nasdaq-100 with mixed reception: shares stumble on debut but analysts see 'tremendous' earnings power.
